projects.title: ATLAS
projects.shortDescription: ATLAS is an internal operations platform for Ruby Red Hospitality’s hotels and restaurants. It brings occupancy forecasts, revenue reporting, guest reviews, food ordering, purchasing, and maintenance into one app with access tailored to each user’s role and property.

children.text: I worked across the full stack on ATLAS, Ruby Red Hospitality’s internal platform for running hotel and restaurant operations across multiple properties. Managers can review occupancy forecasts and daily revenue, monitor guest feedback, order food from a standardized vendor catalog, and track purchase requests and maintenance tasks. Teams can access the app on desktop or install it on their phones.

ATLAS uses Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, with Supabase for PostgreSQL, authentication, and access controls by role and property. The platform processes nightly reports from hotel property management systems to show changes in bookings and year-over-year trends. It also brings sales data from Toast, Square, and Stripe into a shared revenue dashboard and pulls reviews from multiple sites into one place, where teams can review AI-drafted replies.

projects.title: SearchTexasTax
projects.shortDescription: SearchTexasTax is a web app for researching Texas hotel and bar revenue. Built with Next.js, TypeScript, and Supabase, it makes public tax filings searchable by business name, city, county, or ZIP code.

children.text: I worked across the full stack on the new version of SearchTexasTax, a platform that turns public tax filings into a tool for researching Texas hospitality revenue. Users can look up a specific hotel or bar, view its revenue history, or explore trends across a city, county, or ZIP code.

I built the application with Next.js and TypeScript, used Supabase for the database, and set up the data pipelines that retrieve Hotel Occupancy Tax and Mixed Beverage Tax records from the Texas Comptroller. Those pipelines bring the state’s filings into the database that powers the app’s search, property profiles, and revenue charts.

projects.title: WealthCharts
projects.shortDescription: A market research and trading workspace for stocks, ETFs, options, and futures. I led the React refactor and owned frontend code review and merge approvals.

children.text: The product

WealthCharts brings market research, charting, and trade execution into one customizable workspace. Traders can scan stocks, ETFs, options, and futures for setups, save symbols to watchlists, and use chart studies and alerts to track what happens next. They can build custom indicators and backtest strategies with WealthScript. When it’s time to place a trade, they can use paper trading to practice or connect a supported broker to trade live.

The options workspace shows how those tools fit together. A trader can inspect the options chain and Greeks, assemble a multi-leg strategy, and compare how that position responds to changes in the underlying price before previewing an order. WealthThoughts and WealthCharts TV add community discussion and on-demand trading education alongside the research tools.
My role

As Senior Front-End Software Engineer, I led the redesign and React refactor of the flagship web app. I worked on frontend implementation and UX/UI, reviewed changes across the frontend codebase, and approved frontend pushes and merges. That gave me responsibility for how changes to the shared workspace, charting, research, and order workflows fit together before they reached users.
Frontend architecture

The web client was a React single-page application built with JavaScript and TypeScript. React Router handled navigation and Redux Toolkit managed shared state for areas such as watchlists, chart preferences, and broker sessions. FlexLayout provided dockable panels so traders could keep charts, scanners, and order entry in view together. The app prefetched the charting engine in the background, and its frontend integrations handled updates for orders, positions, and balances.

The frontend also used AG Grid for data tables and CodeMirror with a custom WealthScript grammar for strategy editing. Together, these components supported an interface where traders could configure a workspace, work through market data, and write and test strategies from the same application.

projects.title: EnjoySPI
projects.shortDescription: React web application that enhances user experience in room bookings and event reservations, featuring an intuitive user interface integrated with Stripe for secure payments. This application is actively used by major hotel brands such as Hilton, Wyndham, and Marriott.

children.text: EnjoySPI is a dedicated service for vacationers selecting top-tier accommodations on South Padre Island. Built using Next.js and Redux, this React web application significantly enhances the user experience in room bookings and event reservations, featuring an intuitive user interface integrated with Stripe for secure payments. The application is actively used by major hotel brands such as Hilton, Wyndham, and Marriott. EnjoySPI is designed to streamline the vacation booking process, offering users an easy and enjoyable way to book all-inclusive hotel and condo packages. With a focus on user-centric design, the platform ensures that guests can effortlessly navigate through the site, select their preferred accommodation, and complete their booking securely. The integration of modern technologies like Next.js and Redux allows for a seamless and responsive experience across all devices.

As the lead front-end engineer, I developed the EnjoySPI booking platform, focusing on creating an optimal UX/UI. My role involved designing a user-friendly interface, implementing the secure Stripe payment portal, and developing multiple marketing pages to enhance user engagement.
Hotel Information Page

One of the standout features of EnjoySPI is the detailed hotel information pages. Guests can browse through a curated selection of top-rated beachfront hotels on South Padre Island, each offering exclusive packages only available through our platform. The hotel pages provide comprehensive information about the amenities, room types, and on-site services such as bars, restaurants, and concierge services. High-quality images and user reviews from TripAdvisor are incorporated to help guests make informed decisions. Additionally, the hotel page includes a list of available packages at this location, each with detailed descriptions to assist users in making the best choice for their stay.

The page also features a form where users can select their booking dates and the number of guests, ensuring a seamless and personalized booking experience. This interactive form simplifies the reservation process, guiding users step-by-step through selecting the ideal package for their vacation.
Step-by-Step Booking Selection

The booking process on EnjoySPI is designed to be as straightforward as possible. Users start by selecting the number of guests and the duration of their stay. They are then guided through a step-by-step process where they can choose their desired package, select a hotel, and pick a room that suits their needs. Each step is clearly outlined, with helpful prompts and suggestions to ensure that users can complete their booking with ease.
Checkout Form

The checkout process is a critical component of the EnjoySPI platform. Developed using Stripe Elements, our secure payment integration ensures that users can make payments with confidence. The checkout form supports multiple payment methods, including credit or debit cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay, providing flexibility and convenience for users. Additionally, the form allows guests to split payments across multiple cards or payment methods if needed, making it particularly beneficial for group bookings where costs can be shared among multiple travelers. The form is designed to be user-friendly, with clear fields for all necessary information and integrated error handling to ensure a smooth transaction experience.
Event Hosting

In addition to booking vacations, EnjoySPI also offers options for hosting events at specific hotels. Users can book meeting spaces and event venues at top-rated beachfront hotels, such as the Courtyard by Marriott. These venues are perfect for various events, providing detailed information about amenities and services available to ensure a successful event. The event hosting feature includes options for selecting dates, choosing specific amenities, and contacting the hotel directly for further arrangements. This added functionality makes EnjoySPI a versatile platform for both vacationers and event planners.

projects.title: All Inclusive Dashboard
projects.shortDescription: Admin management system built with React.js and Next.js, utilizing Material UI. It enables the management of vacation packages, hotels, condos, reservations, payments, and content, along with a powerful rate-setting tool and media library management.

children.text: The All Inclusive Dashboard is a comprehensive management admin system designed for the All Inclusive projects, such as EnjoySPI. Developed using React.js and Next.js, and leveraging Material UI as a component library, this dashboard provides robust capabilities to manage and streamline various administrative tasks associated with vacation packages.

The All Inclusive Dashboard serves as the backbone for managing all aspects of vacation packages, hotel and condo information, and booking details. It offers an intuitive and powerful interface for administrators to oversee and configure every element required to run a successful vacation booking platform.
Package and Hotel Management

The dashboard allows users to create and manage different vacation packages and associate them with specific hotels and condos. Administrators can easily set up new packages, edit existing ones, and assign accommodations to these packages, ensuring a seamless booking experience for end-users.
Content Management System (CMS)

Featuring a WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) editor, the CMS system within the dashboard empowers users to create and manage single pages on the site effortlessly. This tool ensures that content can be updated quickly and easily without requiring extensive technical knowledge.
Media Library Management

The dashboard includes an in-depth media library management system. Administrators can upload, organize, and manage images, videos, and other media assets. This feature is crucial for maintaining a visually appealing and up-to-date website.
Order and Payment Management

Handling order and payment information is streamlined within the dashboard. Users can view and manage all reservations, track payment statuses, and ensure that all transactions are processed correctly. The system integrates with payment gateways to provide a smooth transaction experience.
Reservation Management

Administrators can access detailed information about hotel reservations, including dates and package details. This feature ensures that all booking information is readily available and can be managed efficiently.
Rate Setting Tool

One of the standout features is the powerful rate setting tool. This tool allows administrators to set different prices for hotel rooms based on various criteria such as nights, weekdays, weeks, or months. It provides extensive options to adjust rates in bulk, ensuring flexibility and efficiency in pricing management.
Coupon Management

The dashboard also includes a feature to create and manage special coupon codes. These coupons can be used on the EnjoySPI website, providing discounts and special offers to users, which can help drive sales and customer engagement.

projects.title: McAllen Education Foundation
projects.shortDescription: WordPress website and grant management tools for the McAllen Education Foundation, a nonprofit that funds classroom projects in McAllen ISD. Educators can apply for grants online, donors can contribute through the site, and the grant committee uses an AI-assisted tool to review proposals.

children.text: I worked on the McAllen Education Foundation’s public website and the systems behind its Innovative Teaching Grants for McAllen ISD educators. Using WordPress and Elementor, I reorganized the site, built pages for grant applications, board members, sponsors, and the annual bowling tournament, and integrated Givebutter for online donations.

For the grant program, I built a Python pipeline that imports Jotform submissions, collects budget attachments, and runs checks against the foundation’s grant rules. I set up the AI review workflow to extract evidence from each proposal, apply the official scoring rubric, and produce preliminary scores and summaries. The pipeline processed 254 applications and flagged cases that needed a closer look. The committee retained responsibility for final funding decisions.

children.text: I created this Game Boy game in GB Studio for VerdeRosa, an exhibition I presented as Emmanuel Con Dos Emmes at Paper Caper Co on South Padre Island, Texas, on April 3, 2026.
The story follows Vero, who feels alone and trapped on the green side. A mysterious entity named Xolotl appears and guides her toward the pink side, where things take on their true forms.

Hi there! I’m Emmanuel, a software engineer and technical lead who’s been building web and mobile applications since 2017. Originally from Veracruz, Mexico, I’ve called Texas home since 2012. I graduated from The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley with a degree in Computer Engineering in 2016.

I’ve always loved video games and computers. I started by making text adventure games in Pascal in high school, then built my first apps in Visual Basic for school projects. That same curiosity still drives me today: I enjoy turning complex problems into useful, intuitive experiences.

These days, I work with React, Next.js, TypeScript, and React Native to build everything from booking and payment platforms to mobile apps and tools for hospitality operations. I’ve led engineering teams, redesigned a trading platform, and built AI-assisted workflows that help people spend less time on repetitive tasks. I also volunteer my technical skills with local nonprofits, helping them use technology to support their communities.
Whether I’m working on a new feature or a whole product, my goal is the same: build things that look great, work even better, and make someone’s day a little easier.
